proposals.before: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.
proposals.after: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.
proposals.reason: Restore the raising of troops and proclamations to provinces and commanderies.

proposals.before: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.
proposals.after: Yao Chengdu, General Who Pacifies the East, resisted him. Yi tried to win Chengdu over with humble words and bind him closely to himself, sending his belt knife as a pledge. Chengdu sent the knife on to Hong.
proposals.reason: Restore Chengdu’s title and Yi’s attempt to bind him personally with a knife from his belt.

proposals.before: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.
proposals.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
proposals.reason: The speaker is Chengdu, the target is Yi, the emperor’s younger full brother (as at s0120). 推轂 signifies the trust of military command. Restore Guo’s office, several hundred armored men, capture and imprisonment, and the dangling-tassel image of peril.

proposals.before: Yi also sent swift cavalry Wang Guo leading several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu; Chengdu seized Guo, imprisoned him, sent reproach to Yi, saying, "The enlightened lord, with mother's-brother closeness, received the charge of the pushing-bar wheel; now the altars' peril hangs like a tassel—he ought reverently to toil in worry and assist the royal house.
proposals.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
proposals.reason: The speaker is Chengdu, the target is Yi, the emperor’s younger full brother (as at s0120). 推轂 signifies the trust of military command. Restore Guo’s office, several hundred armored men, capture and imprisonment, and the dangling-tassel image of peril.

proposals.before: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.
proposals.after: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?
proposals.reason: The speaker charges Yi personally with concealing treachery and scheming against his dynasty; he invokes three ancestors.

proposals.before: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?
proposals.after: This garrison’s grain is the support of the whole region. What merit have your garrison men shown that you would give it to them?
proposals.reason: The whole region depends on this garrison’s grain; Chengdu asks what merit the proposed recipients have earned.

proposals.before: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.
proposals.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
proposals.reason: Guo is the state criminal and the one compared to a man gratuitously adding feet to a snake. Chengdu must await an edict before execution.

proposals.before: Wang Guo was a snake painting feet—a criminal of the state; he is already imprisoned awaiting the edict to execute him.
proposals.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
proposals.reason: Guo is the state criminal and the one compared to a man gratuitously adding feet to a snake. Chengdu must await an edict before execution.

proposals.before: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."
proposals.after: I am now rallying loyal men to punish your crime. When the whole army has assembled, I will meet you on the Yellow River.”
proposals.reason: Restore the object of punishing Yi and the condition that all the forces have assembled.

proposals.before: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.
proposals.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.
proposals.reason: Chengdu addresses the cities, exhorts them to loyal action, prepares weapons and horses, and levies contributions to the cause.

proposals.before: Thereupon he proclaimed to the cities, urged them with loyalty and righteousness, sharpened weapons and fed horses, and levied righteous rent.
proposals.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.
proposals.reason: Chengdu addresses the cities, exhorts them to loyal action, prepares weapons and horses, and levies contributions to the cause.

proposals.before: Thousands in Linjin rose for him.
proposals.after: Several thousand households in Linjin rose in support of Yao Yi.
proposals.reason: 數千戶 counts households, not people.

proposals.before: Yao Shao crossed at Bo ford, crushed the Linjin rebels, and terrified Yao Yi.
proposals.after: Yao Shao crossed at Bo Ford and routed the rebel households of Linjin. Yao Yi and his followers were shaken with fear.
proposals.reason: 懿等 includes others besides Yi.

proposals.before: Guo Chun and Wang Nu besieged Yao Yi.
proposals.after: Guo Chun, Wang Nu and other garrison men from Anding led their followers in surrounding Yao Yi.
proposals.reason: Restore Anding origin, garrison affiliation and leadership of followers in the encirclement.

proposals.before: Yao Shao took Puban, jailed Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang.
proposals.after: Yao Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang and others.
proposals.reason: Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yi, and executed Chang and others.

proposals.before: On New Year's Day Yao Hong wept before his court as Jin closed in and kin rebelled.
proposals.after: With defections at home and abroad and the Jin army drawing nearer, Yao Hong received his ministers in the front hall on New Year’s morning. He shed tears of grief, and the ministers all wept.
proposals.reason: The defections are internal and external, and all the officials wept with Hong at the front-hall audience.

proposals.before: Yao Hui marched on Chang'an with thirty-eight thousand families in chariot fortresses, claiming he would purge evil counselors.
proposals.after: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, burned the houses and led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households toward Chang’an from North Yongzhou, forming his wagons into a square. He styled himself grand commander-in-chief and Great General Who Establishes Righteousness and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies declaring his intent to rid the ruler’s side of evil men.
proposals.reason: Restore the burning of houses, origin in North Yongzhou, square made with wagons, Hui’s self-assumed titles and proclamation to provinces and commanderies.

proposals.before: Jiang Ji rode to his banner.
proposals.after: Jiang Ji, General Who Displays Might, led his men to join Hui.
proposals.reason: Jiang Ji led troops with him and held the Yangwei generalship.

proposals.before: Peng Wandu, who bore credentials, heard that Hui was about to arrive, abandoned Yinmi, and fled back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 建節 is Peng Wandu’s military designation, not an assertion that he carried credentials. Compare the same title on Wang Zong in s0055.

proposals.before: Jianjie Peng Wandu heard Hui would arrive, abandoned Yinmi, fled back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 建節 is Peng Wandu’s military designation, not an assertion that he carried credentials. Compare the same title on Wang Zong in s0055.

proposals.before: Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."
proposals.after: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji urged him, “The state’s leading generals are in the east, leaving the capital undefended. If you strike straight at it with light troops, you are sure to succeed.”
proposals.reason: The exchange takes place when Hui reaches Xinzhi.

proposals.before: Yao Chen lost to Yao Hui; panic gripped Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Hui defeated Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West. Hui’s army gathered still greater strength, and Chang’an was badly shaken.
proposals.reason: Restore Chen’s title and the increase in Hui’s military strength after his victory.

proposals.before: Yao Hong recalled Yao Shao and sent Yao Yu and Hu Yidu west of the Feng River.
proposals.after: Hong sent a rider at speed to summon Yao Shao and ordered Yao Yu and Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to camp west of the Feng River.
proposals.reason: Hong rushed a mounted messenger to recall Shao; Yu and Hu Yidu, who holds the Fuguo title, were to camp west of the Feng.

proposals.before: Several frontier generals went over to Yao Hui.
proposals.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
proposals.reason: Retain all four individuals and their offices, including An’yi protector and Jianwei as a military title, and their fear as motive for surrender.

proposals.before: Fufeng Grand Administrator Yao Jun, Protector of the Pacified Yi Yao Moli, Jianwei Yao E'du, General Who Displays Might Peng Hao all feared and surrendered to Hui.
proposals.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
proposals.reason: Retain all four individuals and their offices, including An’yi protector and Jianwei as a military title, and their fear as motive for surrender.

proposals.before: Yao Hong summoned Gou He and asked, "Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay—how can you alone remain at ease?"
proposals.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
proposals.reason: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He holds the Lijie (立節) generalship, not Jianjie (建節). He remains undivided in his loyalty.

proposals.before: Hui's maternal uncle Gou He then served as Jianjie general, kept loyalty without wavering; Hong summoned him and said, "The multitude all harbor leaving or staying—how can you alone be at ease?"
proposals.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
proposals.reason: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He holds the Lijie (立節) generalship, not Jianjie (建節). He remains undivided in his loyalty.

proposals.before: Gou He said: "If treason wins, uncle and nephew share the stain.
proposals.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness reads 奔馳 for the packet’s 賓士, confirmed independently by the parallel in Shiliuguo chunqiu 61. Gou He means his kinship with Hui does not need to be made closer by hastening to him. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

proposals.before: He said, "If Heaven lets the demon bandit prevail and he gets to carry out his treason, the principle of uncle and nephew needs no guest-retainer to grow closer.
proposals.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness reads 奔馳 for the packet’s 賓士, confirmed independently by the parallel in Shiliuguo chunqiu 61. Gou He means his kinship with Hui does not need to be made closer by hastening to him. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

proposals.before: If Heaven punishes the traitor, a subject stands by his oath.
proposals.after: If instead his crimes reach their limit, his rebellion comes to nothing and Heaven visits its full punishment on him, my duty as a subject is to remain loyal and hold to my resolve.
proposals.reason: Restore the extinction of the rebellion when its guilt has reached its height and the minister’s determination to remain loyal.

proposals.before: Betraying sovereign for kin would shame me."
proposals.after: To turn against my kin or betray my ruler would shame me.”
proposals.reason: The two coordinated phrases are turning against one’s kin and betraying one’s ruler.

proposals.before: Yao Hong honored him with gold seal and purple ribbon.
proposals.after: Hong commended his loyalty and consideration and awarded him a gold seal with a purple ribbon.
proposals.reason: 忠恕 gives Hong’s express commendation of Gou He’s loyalty and consideration.

proposals.before: Yao Shao raced ahead while Yao Qia and Guofan brought thirty thousand foot toward the capital.
proposals.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s light cavalry and distinguish the full compound surname Sima in Sima Guofan; see s0131.

proposals.before: Yao Shao led light horse first to the crisis, sent Yao Qia and Simo Guofan leading thirty thousand foot to hurry to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s light cavalry and distinguish the full compound surname Sima in Sima Guofan; see s0131.

proposals.before: Yao Hui camped at Ducheng; Yao Shao met him at Lingtai.
proposals.after: Yao Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng. He and Yao Shao faced one another at Lingtai.
proposals.reason: Restore Qulao as point of departure and the standoff rather than merely a meeting.

proposals.before: Yao Zan rushed back from Tong Pass, leaving Yin Ya to hold the river.
proposals.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Yin Ya holds the Ningshuo title, is made governor of Hongnong and guards Tong Pass. Zan leads his armies back on hearing that Hui is drawing near.

proposals.before: When Zan heard Hui pressed gradually, he left Ningyin Yin Ya as Hongnong grand administrator guarding Tong Pass, led all armies back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Yin Ya holds the Ningshuo title, is made governor of Hongnong and guards Tong Pass. Zan leads his armies back on hearing that Hui is drawing near.

proposals.before: Yao Hong told Yao Zan: "I have failed the ancestors and shamed my uncles with these kin revolts.
proposals.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.
proposals.reason: 謝 is an acknowledgment of fault here. Yuanzi blames his failure to lead by virtue for the troubles within his own house and rebellion among his brothers.

proposals.before: Hong thanked Zan, saying, "Yuanzi cannot brighten virtue and righteousness or lead the host below, causing disaster to rise from the inner wall and change to come from same-blood kin—already above I fail the ancestors, below I have no face to see the uncles.
proposals.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.
proposals.reason: 謝 is an acknowledgment of fault here. Yuanzi blames his failure to lead by virtue for the troubles within his own house and rebellion among his brothers.

proposals.before: Yao Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers seemed weak and had no means to check them."
proposals.after: Yao Zan replied, “Yi and the others dared take up arms and attack us from within surely because we, your ministers, are weak and had no means of forestalling or checking them.”
proposals.reason: Zan admits the ministers’ weakness, rather than saying they only seemed weak.

proposals.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject and the grand general will not destroy these bandits—I shall never again show my face before Your Majesty!"
proposals.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”
proposals.reason: 不滅此賊 is the condition of Zan’s vow, not a prediction that he and the grand general will fail. 攘袂 is pushing up the sleeves.

proposals.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject with the grand general will not destroy these bandits—never again shall I hold face to see Your Majesty!"
proposals.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”
proposals.reason: 不滅此賊 is the condition of Zan’s vow, not a prediction that he and the grand general will fail. 攘袂 is pushing up the sleeves.

proposals.before: Yao Hong paid the troops and sent them out.
proposals.after: Yao Hong distributed gifts to the soldiers and sent them off.
proposals.reason: 班賜 means distributing gifts or rewards, not paying wages.

proposals.before: Yao Hui's men wavered; Qi Huang and others defected.
proposals.after: When Hui’s men saw that the armies had all assembled, fear seized them and they began to think of returning to allegiance. His general Qi Huang and others abandoned him and surrendered.
proposals.reason: Restore the sight of the assembled armies, universal fear and reconsideration, and that Qi Huang and others were Hui’s generals.

proposals.before: Yao Zan fell on Yao Hui from the rear, killed him and three brothers.
proposals.after: As Hui advanced against Shao, Zan intercepted him from the rear and routed him, killing Hui and his three younger brothers.
proposals.reason: Restore Hui’s advance on Shao, Zan’s decisive rout and the three brothers as younger brothers.

proposals.before: Yao Hong buried him with princely honors and mourned bitterly.
proposals.after: Yao Hong wept bitterly for Hui and buried him with the rites of a duke.
proposals.reason: 公 specifies the ducal rank of the funeral rites.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.
proposals.reason: Xiangyi is a stockade; Jianwei is Xue Bo’s generalship.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.
proposals.reason: Xiangyi is a stockade; Jianwei is Xue Bo’s generalship.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji crossed north against Puban; Gou Zhuo lost to Yao Chengdu at Xiongnu Fort.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness has 自陜 for 白陝. Restore Daoji’s departure from Shan, his order to General Gou Zhuo, and that it was Zhuo who was defeated at Xiongnu Fort. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

proposals.before: Daoji crossed north from Shan, attacked Puban, sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort, and was defeated by Hong's General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness has 自陜 for 白陝. Restore Daoji’s departure from Shan, his order to General Gou Zhuo, and that it was Zhuo who was defeated at Xiongnu Fort. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Lü to Puban and Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yao Lü to relieve Puban, while Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: 救 is the specific mission to relieve Puban.

proposals.before: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.
proposals.after: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.
proposals.reason: 太宰 is grand minister, distinct from grand tutor. Restore every new appointment and the retained attendants’, inspector’s and clan offices, staff of authority and oversight of the Secretariat. 大政 encompasses major court policy beyond war.

proposals.before: Hong advanced Shao to grand tutor, grand general, grand commander-in-chief, commander of all military affairs within and without, granted yellow battle-axe, changed enfeoffment to duke of Lu—palace attendant, director of Sizhou, director of clan affairs, holding seal and tallies as before; great court policy all went to decide there.
proposals.after: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.
proposals.reason: 太宰 is grand minister, distinct from grand tutor. Restore every new appointment and the retained attendants’, inspector’s and clan offices, staff of authority and oversight of the Secretariat. 大政 encompasses major court policy beyond war.

proposals.before: He sent Yao Shao with fifty thousand men to Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yao Shao, with Martial Guard commander Yao Luan and others, at the head of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose the Jin army at Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Restore Luan’s role, the combined infantry and cavalry, and the purpose of opposing Jin at the pass.

proposals.before: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao hit Tan Daoji from two sides.
proposals.after: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao, inspector of Bingzhou, coordinated their forces inside and outside the defenses and attacked Tan Daoji from both sides.
proposals.reason: Restore Yin Zhao’s inspectorate of Bingzhou and the coordination of the two forces inside and out.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji, saying, "Puban is walled and moated too strong for a quick assault; attacking bleeds the army, holding it wastes days. Abandon it and strike Tong Pass first.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji stayed behind his fortifications and declined battle. Shen Linzi urged him, “Puban’s walls are strong and its moat is deep. We cannot take it quickly. An assault would cost us men, and waiting here would waste days. Better abandon it and turn first to Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Restore Daoji’s refusal of battle behind his defenses before Linzi offers advice.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji gave up Puban and marched on Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji followed his advice, abandoned Puban and headed south toward Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: 從之 identifies the adoption of Linzi’s advice, and the march was south.

proposals.before: Yao Zan took seven thousand palace guards to Pu ford.
proposals.after: Yao Zan led seven thousand palace guards east from north of the Wei River and advanced to occupy Pu Ford.
proposals.reason: Restore the eastward march from north of the Wei and the occupation of the ford.

proposals.before: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo; towns collapsed toward the capital.
proposals.after: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo with more than ten thousand men. In many places people abandoned their cities and garrisons and fled to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore the ten-thousand-plus force, and make clear that people abandoned towns and fled to Chang’an.

proposals.before: Shen Tianzi reached Qingni while Yao Shao advanced to face Tan Daoji.
proposals.after: Shen Tianzi and the others advanced as far as Qingni, while Yao Shao advanced in square formation to bar Tan Daoji’s way.
proposals.reason: Restore Tianzi’s companions and Shao’s square formation.

proposals.before: Daoji led Wang Chong, Shen Linzi and others to charge straight at Shao's army; officers and soldiers startled and scattered, drew back to Dingcheng.
proposals.after: Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi and others in a charge against Shao’s army. Shao’s officers and men scattered in alarm and fell back to Dingcheng.
proposals.reason: The name in both this unit and s0222 is 王敬 (Wang Jing), not Wang Chong. Shao’s men are the ones who scatter.

proposals.before: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to choke Tan Daoji's supply line.
proposals.after: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to hold the narrows and cut Tan Daoji’s grain route.
proposals.reason: 守險 is holding a strategic position in order to cut the supply route.

proposals.before: Liu Yu's columns entered from Ziwu and Luogu valleys.
proposals.after: Liu Yu’s detachment commanders Yao Zhen and Dou Ba led separate forces of several thousand men each, Yao Zhen entering by Ziwu and Dou Ba by Luogu.
proposals.reason: Restore both commanders’ names, their different routes and the several thousand men under each.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan and Yao Qiang to meet them.
proposals.after: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan to oppose Dou Ba and Yao Qiang to oppose Yao Zhen.
proposals.reason: The order names Wan’s opponent as Dou Ba and Qiang’s as Yao Zhen.

proposals.before: Yin Ya was captured by Xu Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: Yao Luan sent his general Yin Ya against Xu Yan, Tan Daoji’s major, south of Tong Pass. Xu Yan captured Yin Ya and sent him to Liu Yu.
proposals.reason: Restore Luan’s dispatch of his general, Xu Yan’s office under Daoji and the encounter’s location.

proposals.before: Yin Ya said: "You spared me once; now I will not beg like a coward.
proposals.after: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?
proposals.reason: 寧不甘心 is a rhetorical affirmative: Ya is willing to die since his earlier survival had already exceeded his hopes. Neither a previous act of clemency by Liu Yu nor cowardice is stated. The parallel Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 至今死固甘心.

proposals.before: Ya said, "Formerly living was already beyond expectation; now death surely I do not willingly accept.
proposals.after: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?
proposals.reason: 寧不甘心 is a rhetorical affirmative: Ya is willing to die since his earlier survival had already exceeded his hopes. Neither a previous act of clemency by Liu Yu nor cowardice is stated. The parallel Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 至今死固甘心.

proposals.before: You claim to conquer by virtue—do not kill the one Qin man who keeps faith!"
proposals.after: You intend to pacify the realm through great righteousness. How can you deny Qin a minister who keeps faith with his ruler?”
proposals.reason: Ya asks how Liu Yu could deny Qin the right to have loyal servants; he does not claim to be its only loyal man.

proposals.before: Yao Hong posted Yao Hedou at Yaoliu against Shen Tianzi.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.
proposals.reason: Restore Hedu’s court office. 和都 is Hedu (都, dū), not Hedou; he recurs in s0207 and s0223.

proposals.before: Hong sent attendant gentleman Huangmen Yao Hedou to camp at Yaoliu to prepare for Tianzi.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.
proposals.reason: Restore Hedu’s court office. 和都 is Hedu (都, dū), not Hedou; he recurs in s0207 and s0223.

proposals.before: Yao Shao told his generals: "Jin hugs its walls waiting for reinforcements.
proposals.after: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.
proposals.reason: 送死 means they have come to their deaths, not to deliver death. Shao notes their long march and small numbers and explains their defensive delay.

proposals.before: Yao Shao said to the generals, "Daoji and others have come from afar to deliver death; their hosts are not many; hugging ramparts and self-fortifying—they only wish to prolong days and months to await follow-up relief.
proposals.after: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.
proposals.reason: 送死 means they have come to their deaths, not to deliver death. Shao notes their long march and small numbers and explains their defensive delay.

proposals.before: Send a column to Wenxiang to sever their supplies and Tan Daoji's head will be on your pole within a month.
proposals.after: I want to send part of our army back to hold Wenxiang and cut their grain transport. Before a month has passed, Daoji’s head can hang beneath my standard.
proposals.reason: Shao proposes dividing his own force and sending it back to occupy Wenxiang; 麾下 is under his standard, not the hearer’s pole.

proposals.before: Kill Tan Daoji and Liu Yu loses his spear point."
proposals.after: Once Daoji and the others are destroyed, Liu Yu’s plans will come to nothing.”
proposals.reason: The prediction concerns Daoji and his companions and the consequent frustration of Liu Yu’s plans.

proposals.before: Yao Shao spread his wings: Hu Yidu on the east plain, Yao Luan on the main road, pressing Jin.
proposals.after: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.
proposals.reason: Shao disposes forces along different routes in mutually supporting positions; both named generals’ offices and their proximity to the Jin army belong to that deployment.

proposals.before: Shao divided roads and set various armies in horn-and-flank posture, sent General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to hold the eastern plain, Martial Guard Yao Luan to camp on the great road, connecting with the Jin army.
proposals.after: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.
proposals.reason: Shao disposes forces along different routes in mutually supporting positions; both named generals’ offices and their proximity to the Jin army belong to that deployment.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi night-attacked; Yao Luan fell with nine thousand men.
proposals.after: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.
proposals.reason: 銜枚 is silencing soldiers with mouth gags for the surprise raid. Luan’s troops rout, Luan is killed in battle, and more than nine thousand soldiers die.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi picked crack troops, held mouthpieces for a night raid; Luan's host broke in battle and died; more than nine thousand soldiers died.
proposals.after: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.
proposals.reason: 銜枚 is silencing soldiers with mouth gags for the surprise raid. Luan’s troops rout, Luan is killed in battle, and more than nine thousand soldiers die.

proposals.before: Yao Zan tried to ship grain from Puban but Jin smashed the train at Xiangcheng.
proposals.after: Yao Zan camped on the Yellow River and sent Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, to bring grain from Puban to supply his army. When Nan reached Xiangcheng, the Jin army defeated him.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan’s camp on the Yellow River, the dispatch of General Yao Nan with the grain, and Nan as the defeated commander.

proposals.before: Yao Chen raced to save Yao Nan, missed him, but beat a Jin column in the bend and held Puban.
proposals.after: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.
proposals.reason: Chen guards Yaoliu. Hedu is the active commander in Hedong and hurries to Nan, then defeats the subordinate and camps at Puban. 兼道 is forced marching. proposals.before: At the time Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu, Yao Hedou campaigned against Xue Bo in Hedong; hearing the royal army was intercepting Nan, they hurried by combined roads to rescue; before arriving Nan was defeated, yet they broke Liu Yu's lieutenant at the river bend, then camped at Puban.
proposals.after: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.

proposals.before: Yao Shao sent Yao Qia to Jiuyuan to choke Tan Daoji's supply convoys.
proposals.after: Yao Shao sent his left chief clerk Yao Qia, Yao Moli and others with three thousand cavalry to camp at Jiuyuan north of the Yellow River. He meant to cut off the tax-grain shipments that the counties were sending Tan Daoji.
proposals.reason: The detachment includes left chief clerk Qia, Moli and others with three thousand horse. Jiuyuan lies north of the Yellow River; the supplies are county tax shipments for Daoji.

proposals.before: Yao Qia refused: "A small force that stands stubborn becomes bait.
proposals.after: Yao Qia objected, “A small force that stands its ground becomes the captive of a larger enemy.
proposals.reason: The warning is that stubborn resistance makes a small force the captive of a large enemy, not bait for it.

proposals.before: We are too few and too far—even you cannot stretch a whip across the river."
proposals.after: Our troops are few and weak, far away beyond the Yellow River. For all your military prowess, my lord, your whip is short and the forces unequal. I fear you will be unable to reach us.”
proposals.reason: Restore Qia’s praise of Shao, the force imbalance and his fear that relief could not reach them.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi destroyed Yao Qia on the riverbank.
proposals.after: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.
proposals.reason: Linzi led eight thousand men, not eight thousand armies; Qia died in battle and all his force was lost.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi led eight thousand hosts, intercepted Qia on the river; Qia died in battle, the host all perished.
proposals.after: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.
proposals.reason: Linzi led eight thousand men, not eight thousand armies; Qia died in battle and all his force was lost.

proposals.before: Yao Shao died of rage and bleeding after Yao Qia's loss.
proposals.after: When Yao Shao learned of the defeat of Yao Qia and the others, his anger brought on an illness. He entrusted affairs to Yao Zan and sent Yao Nan to encamp west of the pass. Shao vomited blood and died.
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s illness, entrusting affairs to Zan, sending Nan west of the pass, and vomiting blood.

proposals.before: Yao Hong begged Northern Wei for aid against Jin.
proposals.after: As the Jin army pressed closer, Yao Hong sent envoys to Wei to ask for troops.
proposals.reason: Hong made the request by sending envoys; he sought troops.

proposals.before: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng to occupy Henei and Hedong as support for Yao Hong.
proposals.after: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.
proposals.reason: Two dukes advance into Henei. Wang Luosheng alone is assigned Hedong. The literal instead implies that all three occupied Henei; the idiomatic conflates the assignments.

proposals.before: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng; they advanced to occupy Henei, and Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong, as sounding support for Hong.
proposals.after: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.
proposals.reason: Two dukes advance into Henei. Wang Luosheng alone is assigned Hedong. The literal instead implies that all three occupied Henei; the idiomatic conflates the assignments.

proposals.before: Liu Yu halted at Shan city and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops over the mountains to join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, intending to attack Yaoliu.
proposals.after: Liu Yu halted at the city of Shan and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand picked troops to open a route across the mountains. They were to join Shen Tianzi and the others at Qingni for an attack on Yaoliu.
proposals.reason: 越山開道 includes opening a route across the mountains.

proposals.before: Yao Hong marched with Yao Yu to meet them.
proposals.after: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu ahead with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose them. Hong himself led the main army out after him.
proposals.reason: Restore Yu’s separate eight-thousand-strong force and Hong’s personal departure afterward at the head of the main army.

proposals.before: Yao Yu lost to Shen Tianzi; Yao Hong fell back to Bashang as towns went over to Jin.
proposals.after: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.
proposals.reason: 郡縣 covers both commanderies and counties, and 潛通 means secret contact, not open submission.

proposals.before: Yu was defeated by Tianzi; Hong drew back to camp at Bashang; many Guanzhong counties secretly communicated with the royal army.
proposals.after: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.
proposals.reason: 郡縣 covers both commanderies and counties, and 潛通 means secret contact, not open submission.

proposals.before: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.
proposals.after: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.
proposals.reason: 徐猗之 is the full name Xu Yizhi, confirmed by 猗之 repeated twice at s0223.

proposals.before: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass, sent generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.
proposals.after: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.
proposals.reason: 徐猗之 is the full name Xu Yizhi, confirmed by 猗之 repeated twice at s0223.

proposals.before: Yao Zan faced Liu Yu; Yao Nan held Xiangcheng.
proposals.after: Yao Zan opposed Liu Yu west of the pass, and Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.
proposals.reason: Zan opposed Yu west of the pass.

proposals.before: Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Chong west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
proposals.after: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen’e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei and press Yao Nan’s army.
proposals.reason: 王敬 is Wang Jing, as at s0187.

proposals.before: Yao Pu crushed Jin at Puban; Xu Yi died and Zhu Chaoshi ran.
proposals.after: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Both Yao Pu and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi’s party; 鎮東 is General Who Guards the East. Restore Yizhi’s full name as at s0220 and Chaoshi’s abandonment of his troops and flight to Tong Pass.

proposals.before: General Who Conquers the East Yao Pu and Yao Hedou defeated Yi and others at Puban; Yi met death; Chaoshi abandoned his host and fled to Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Both Yao Pu and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi’s party; 鎮東 is General Who Guards the East. Restore Yizhi’s full name as at s0220 and Chaoshi’s abandonment of his troops and flight to Tong Pass.

proposals.before: Floods blocked Yao Zan from crossing the Wei.
proposals.after: Heavy rains sent the Wei River over its banks, and Yao Zan and the others could not cross to the north.
proposals.reason: Continuous heavy rain made the Wei overflow, preventing Zan and his companions from crossing north.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e overtook Yao Nan in the flood season.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e advanced by water and by land and overtook Yao Nan.
proposals.reason: 水陸兼進 means a coordinated advance by land and water, not an observation about flood season.

proposals.before: Yao Hong rushed to Stone Bridge to help.
proposals.after: Hong brought his army back from Bashang and halted at Stone Bridge to support Yao Nan.
proposals.reason: Hong returns with his army from Bashang, camps at the bridge, and intends to aid Nan.

proposals.before: Yao Zan fell back to Zheng.
proposals.after: Yao Zan withdrew and encamped at the city of Zheng.
proposals.reason: 退屯 is withdrawal to camp at the specified city.

proposals.before: Yao Qiang joined Yao Nan on the Jing River line.
proposals.after: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.
proposals.reason: 鎮北 is General Who Guards the North. Restore Qiang’s several thousand local men, formation on the Jing with Nan, and objective against Zhen’e.

proposals.before: General Who Conquers the North Yao Qiang led several thousand commandery people and with Yao Nan formed array on the Jing to block Zhen'e.
proposals.after: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.
proposals.reason: 鎮北 is General Who Guards the North. Restore Qiang’s several thousand local men, formation on the Jing with Nan, and objective against Zhen’e.

proposals.before: Mao Dezu killed Yao Qiang; Yao Nan bolted for Chang'an.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e sent Mao Dezu against Yao Qiang and routed him. Qiang died in battle, and Yao Nan fled back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Zhen’e orders Dezu’s attack, which routs Qiang. Qiang dies fighting; no individual killer is identified.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
proposals.reason: 夾渭 specifies the advance on both banks before the defeat at Wei Bridge.

proposals.before: Yao Hong's relief column stampeded itself in the narrow river flats.
proposals.after: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s point of departure, his attempt to aid Pi, Pi’s defeat, and the trampling in retreat.

proposals.before: Yao Chen and forward army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.
proposals.after: Yao Chen, Yao Lie of the Vanguard, Yao Bao’an of the Left Guard, Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo, Yao Jin, General Who Establishes Martial Might, Yao Hao, General Who Displays Might, Sun Xuan, right assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and others all died in battle. Hong returned to the palace alone on horseback.
proposals.reason: 建武 is Jianwu, not Jianwei. Restore Sun Xuan’s department and the military and court designations of the fallen.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e broke Pingshuo Gate; Yao Hong fled toward Stone Bridge.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.
proposals.reason: Zhen’e entered through the gate; no breaking of the gate is reported. Restore Yao Yu and the several hundred horsemen fleeing with Hong.

proposals.before: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.
proposals.after: When Yao Zan learned of Hong’s defeat, he summoned his officers and men and told them. They all struck the ground with their knives, pushed up their sleeves and wept aloud.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan as recipient and messenger of the news, the knives, the sleeve gesture and the loud weeping.

proposals.before: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu. That day he abandoned his men and fled to Yu.
proposals.reason: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu and deserted his troops that day.

proposals.before: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.
proposals.after: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan’s night march to meet Hong at Stone Bridge, Jin’s control of the gates and his men’s dispersal.

proposals.before: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: At a loss for any other plan, Yao Hong considered surrendering to Liu Yu.
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s inability to devise any other plan and his deliberation about surrender.

proposals.before: His eleven-year-old son Yao Fonian said: "Surrender will not save us—better to die cleanly."
proposals.after: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The Jin men will have their way, and in the end they surely will not spare you. I beg you to take your own life.”
proposals.reason: The eleven-year-old addresses Hong, warning that Jin will have its way and will not spare him. 願自裁決 urges suicide, not permission to decide for the child. The parallel in Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 不如引決 and Hu Sanxing glosses it as 自裁.

proposals.before: His son Fonian, age eleven, said to Hong, "The Jin people will indulge their desires to the end—you will surely not be preserved whole; I wish to decide for myself."
proposals.after: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The Jin men will have their way, and in the end they surely will not spare you. I beg you to take your own life.”
proposals.reason: The eleven-year-old addresses Hong, warning that Jin will have its way and will not spare him. 願自裁決 urges suicide, not permission to decide for the child. The parallel in Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 不如引決 and Hu Sanxing glosses it as 自裁.

proposals.before: Yao Hong could not answer.
proposals.after: Yao Hong was stricken and gave no answer.
proposals.reason: 憮然 describes Hong’s distress; 不答 says he did not answer, not that he was unable.

proposals.before: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.
proposals.after: Yao Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself to his death.
proposals.reason: Restore climbing the wall and dying of his deliberate fall.

proposals.before: Yao Hong brought his family to Liu Yu's camp and yielded.
proposals.after: Yao Hong took his wife and children to the gate of Liu Yu’s camp and surrendered.
proposals.reason: 妻子 explicitly identifies his wife and children, and he went to the camp gate.

proposals.before: Liu Yu slaughtered the surrendered Yao princes and deported the clan to the south.
proposals.after: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan leading over a hundred younger imperial clansmen to surrender, the killing of them all, and the distinct fate of the remaining clan south of the Yangtze.

proposals.before: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.
proposals.after: Yao Hong was sent to Jiankang and beheaded in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had reigned for two years.
proposals.reason: The account describes Hong’s conveyance to Jiankang and execution by beheading specifically.

proposals.before: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.
proposals.after: Historical Appraisal
proposals.reason: 史評 is the heading itself; translate it instead of describing its editorial function.

proposals.after: Historical Appraisal
proposals.reason: 史評 is the heading itself; translate it instead of describing its editorial function.

proposals.before: The historian opens: age of warlords and tribal armies without end.
proposals.after: The court historian says: Since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince who became a dragon founded the dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and never been quiet. Warhorses have galloped back and forth without rest. Thick murk darkened the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
proposals.reason: 徙御 is the removal of the imperial court, not its defense. 化龍 invokes the crossing and accession of Jin’s founder in the south (the rhyme in Jinshu 6). Restore the unrest, the warhorses, darkness, floods, Heaven and the multitude of violent armies.

proposals.before: The historiographer says: From moving the defense to the Yangtze, transforming dragon and founding enterprise, great bandits seized the chance and were not yet quiet; war-horses galloped one upon another without rest; heavy murk veiled the six deserts, great floods drummed the eight bounds—Heaven had not tired of chaos, and fierce hosts were truly many.
proposals.after: The court historian says: Since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince who became a dragon founded the dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and never been quiet. Warhorses have galloped back and forth without rest. Thick murk darkened the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
proposals.reason: 徙御 is the removal of the imperial court, not its defense. 化龍 invokes the crossing and accession of Jin’s founder in the south (the rhyme in Jinshu 6). Restore the unrest, the warhorses, darkness, floods, Heaven and the multitude of violent armies.

proposals.before: Yao Yizhong defied Shi Hu yet sought peace—his loyalty earns praise.
proposals.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke with uncompromising frankness to a violent ruler and set forth the counsels of loyalty at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
proposals.reason: 金方 is the west; Yizhong gave allegiance to the Shi and spoke frankly to their violent ruler. His dying counsel was submission to Jin, explicit in Jinshu 116, 我死，汝便歸晉. 鳴哀 evokes his final words.

proposals.before: Yizhong crossed from the metal quarter, spoke of returning to the Shi house, raised straight words to a violent lord, spread loyal instruction in a perilous court—his plan for posterity lay in submission; the meaning of his lament is worth praising.
proposals.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke with uncompromising frankness to a violent ruler and set forth the counsels of loyalty at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
proposals.reason: 金方 is the west; Yizhong gave allegiance to the Shi and spoke frankly to their violent ruler. His dying counsel was submission to Jin, explicit in Jinshu 116, 我死，汝便歸晉. 鳴哀 evokes his final words.

proposals.before: Yao Xiang matched Sun Ce in dash but marched into tragedy.
proposals.after: Yao Xiang, called Jingguo, showed exceptional courage and talent from his youth and was compared to Sun Ce. A close look at his ability and judgment bears out the comparison. That he went on to take a mistaken path is indeed cause for sorrow.
proposals.reason: 景國 identifies Xiang by his courtesy name. Restore the comparison made in his youth, the judgment on his ability and the historian’s lament for his misguided course.

proposals.before: Yao Chang took up Yao Xiang's legacy, stepped into Fu Jian's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise, and borrowed Murong Chong's edge to settle Hangu and Qin.
proposals.after: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.
proposals.reason: 仲襄 refers jointly to Yizhong and Xiang, father and elder brother of Chang, not a person named Zhongxiang or Xiang alone. 容沖 is Murong Chong. Preserve both named regions in the parallel. Cf. Jinshu 116.

proposals.before: Jingmao took up Zhongxiang's thread, stepped into Fu's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise—borrowed Chong's edge to bow and settle Han and Qin;
proposals.after: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.
proposals.reason: 仲襄 refers jointly to Yizhong and Xiang, father and elder brother of Chang, not a person named Zhongxiang or Xiang alone. 容沖 is Murong Chong. Preserve both named regions in the parallel. Cf. Jinshu 116.

proposals.before: He broke Murong Chui's power and quieted the northeast.
proposals.after: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.reason: 雷惡 abbreviates Lei Edi, not Murong Chui; Jinshu 116 places Lei Edi’s attack in the northeast and narrates its defeat.

proposals.before: broke the point of Lei E, brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.after: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.reason: 雷惡 abbreviates Lei Edi, not Murong Chui; Jinshu 116 places Lei Edi’s attack in the northeast and narrates its defeat.

proposals.before: He marked new camps with trees—passing as order.
proposals.after: The rows of trees that marked his new camp may indeed be called a record of achievement.
proposals.reason: This refers to planting trees to commemorate a military victory at the camp, described in Jinshu 116: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功. 效績 concedes an accomplishment.

proposals.before: Planting trees to mark new camps—though called achievement;
proposals.after: The rows of trees that marked his new camp may indeed be called a record of achievement.
proposals.reason: This refers to planting trees to commemorate a military victory at the camp, described in Jinshu 116: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功. 效績 concedes an accomplishment.

proposals.before: Yet he trampled his old lord Fu Jian—heartless.
proposals.after: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!
proposals.reason: 薦棘 is literally laying the exhumed body of Chang’s former lord Fu Jian on thorns. Jinshu 116 states 萇乃掘苻堅屍 … 薦之以棘. 陵 denotes maltreatment or humiliation.

proposals.before: pushing brambles to climb the old lord—how lacking in benevolence!
proposals.after: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!
proposals.reason: 薦棘 is literally laying the exhumed body of Chang’s former lord Fu Jian on thorns. Jinshu 116 states 萇乃掘苻堅屍 … 薦之以棘. 陵 denotes maltreatment or humiliation.

proposals.before: Yao Xing broke strong enemies, finished his father's work, sought wise counsel, knit his clan, and ruled with clear rewards—rivaling Zhuang of Chu or Mu of Qin.
proposals.after: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.
proposals.reason: Restore the full progression through Xing’s predecessor, consultations, recruitment of worthy men, family relationships, paired rewards and punishments, and the loyalty and sacrifice of officers and warriors. The comparison with Chu and Qin belongs to s0261.

proposals.before: Zilue was able to crush mighty foes, bore the completed prior structure, emptied breast to visit the Way, set aside mat to seek worthies, thickly befriended younger brothers to harmonize kin, clarified rewards and punishments to face those below—heroes exhausted their integrity, claws and fangs gave their lives.
proposals.after: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.
proposals.reason: Restore the full progression through Xing’s predecessor, consultations, recruitment of worthy men, family relationships, paired rewards and punishments, and the loyalty and sacrifice of officers and warriors. The comparison with Chu and Qin belongs to s0261.

proposals.before: At his height he held the heartland and the west in prosperity few could match.
proposals.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
proposals.reason: Restore Fen, Jiang, Xu, Luo, Yan, Shu, Longyou, Hexi, prosperous livelihoods, good harvests and unity near and far. The concluding comparison with King Zhuang and Duke Mu belongs here. 藩 means bringing Shu into vassalage.

proposals.before: He took Fen and Jiang, fell Xu and Luo, treated false Yan as vassal and hedged false Shu, leveled Longyou and quieted Hexi—customs rich, years abundant, far quieted and near gathered—though Chu Zhuang or Qin Mu, how could they surpass!
proposals.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
proposals.reason: Restore Fen, Jiang, Xu, Luo, Yan, Shu, Longyou, Hexi, prosperous livelihoods, good harvests and unity near and far. The concluding comparison with King Zhuang and Duke Mu belongs here. 藩 means bringing Shu into vassalage.

proposals.before: Then pride undid his caution.
proposals.after: Afterward he gave free rein to his ambitions and boasted of his achievements, taking no thought for future trouble.
proposals.reason: Restore indulgence of ambition, boasting of achievement and neglect of future dangers.

proposals.before: He entrusted Liangzhou to Tufa, handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity; inner walls rose again and again; war without quiet years, men harbored peril in heart.
proposals.after: He entrusted the capital of Liang to Tufa and granted Shuofang to Helian. His insistence on having his way bred disasters. Frontier cities fell in succession, and his rejection of remonstrance invited calamity. Trouble repeatedly broke out within his own house. There was no year of respite from warfare, and the people felt themselves in danger.
proposals.reason: 涼都 is the capital of Liang, not the entire Liangzhou; 蕭牆屢發 refers to troubles repeatedly breaking out within the ruling house.

proposals.before: He should have showered his soldiers with thanks—
proposals.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?
proposals.reason: Retain Xing’s grand ambitions and the favor due to his armored warriors; the rhetorical thought turns to his contrary choice at s0265.

proposals.before: How fitting to ride those heroic plans and spread deep favor on armored men—
proposals.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?
proposals.reason: Retain Xing’s grand ambitions and the favor due to his armored warriors; the rhetorical thought turns to his contrary choice at s0265.

proposals.before: —yet he lavished gold on Buddhist monks instead.
proposals.after: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
proposals.reason: No gold is specified. The historian condemns deceptive teachings and extraordinary honors for Buddhist monks.

proposals.before: He let monasteries swell while taxes bled the hills.
proposals.after: At a time that demanded action he devoted himself to the pursuit of nonaction. Those clad in fine robes and fed on rich food numbered nearly ten thousand. Analyzing the real and discoursing on emptiness became the general fashion.
proposals.reason: Restore the antithesis of action and nonaction, the nearly ten thousand richly dressed and fed people, and widespread discussion of the Buddhist doctrine of emptiness. No hillside taxation occurs until s0269.

proposals.before: Even the vast Han court scorned the waste of the Hongdu academy.
proposals.after: Even under the wealthy and far-reaching Han dynasty, the expense of the Hongdu academy drew scorn.
proposals.reason: The criticism of spending on Hongdu occurs despite the wealth and extent of the Han; the sentence need not make the Han court itself the critic.

proposals.before: How much less could a shrinking rebel realm bear endless monastic extravagance?
proposals.after: How, then, could a regime whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the construction work at Yonggui?
proposals.reason: 永貴 is the Yonggui ward, where Xing built a Buddhist stupa (Jinshu 117, 起浮圖於永貴裏). The rhetorical question concerns that specific construction project.

proposals.before: Empty treasuries and forest levies—not fate but policy destroyed Later Qin.
proposals.after: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.
proposals.reason: Restore depleted stores, taxation of hills as well as forests, neglected government and loss of authority, which the historian ties to collective downfall.

proposals.before: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.
proposals.after: Yao Hong, called Yuanzi, was mediocre and timid. He came to power in the aftermath of upheaval, and as internal troubles intensified, defense against outside enemies ceased.
proposals.reason: The focus is Hong’s timidity amid preceding upheavals and the suspension of external defense as internal crises grew. The original does not mention a discrete Jin strike here.

proposals.before: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;
proposals.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 杖順 describes relying on the justice of the cause; 弭節 describes an unhurried advance, and 下長安 the taking of Chang’an.

proposals.before: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;
proposals.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 杖順 describes relying on the justice of the cause; 弭節 describes an unhurried advance, and 下長安 the taking of Chang’an.

proposals.before: the last heir bound himself at Zhidao.
proposals.after: The ill-fated heir had no plan left and surrendered at Zhidao with the cord of submission about his neck.
proposals.reason: Restore the condemned heir’s loss of a plan and actual surrender, with the cord as its sign. The wording evokes the surrender of Qin at Zhidao.

proposals.before: Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Chang alone was a treacherous champion.
proposals.after: Xiang was indeed heroic and resolute; Chang was an outstanding man of treachery.
proposals.reason: 惟 is an emphatic connective introducing Chang’s characterization; it does not say that only Chang was treacherous.

proposals.before: Yao Xing first raised the frame; Yao Hong was then destroyed and extinguished.
proposals.after: Under Xing the dynastic edifice rose high; under Hong it came crashing down.
proposals.reason: The paired verse describes the rise and fall of the dynastic structure under Xing and Hong; the object carried forward is the house, rather than Hong’s personal destruction alone.

proposals.before: Let later ages shun that fatal road.
proposals.after: Let this stand as a warning to those who come after: do not follow the same perilous tracks.
